current.text: He is a projected starter for Atlanta, next to McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Okongwu. Each starter is expected to play 30 or more minutes.
Lu Dort is the main threat to his minutes. Dort and Daniels will play together some but will mostly be staggered for spacing.
Experts expect him to keep his starting job over Dort. If Dort starts, it would more likely be in place of McCollum. He is seen as the better defender, and Luke Kennard is not seen as a threat.
He shot about 18% from three last season, after about 34% the season before. He shot over 30% from three over the last six weeks of the season.
Experts expect both his three-point shooting and his steals to improve this season. They see little downside. Steals targets range from about 2.3 to close to three per game.
In Atlanta's scheme after the Trae Young trade, he rebounded much more and at times played almost a big man role on offense.

Experts rate him well above his ADP of about 60. Targets range from pick 43 to around 50, roughly round four. They call his low rank an overreaction to him going far too high last season. Josh thinks the whole Atlanta backcourt is undervalued by 20 to 30 spots. His draft position varies a lot from draft to draft.
In auctions he is worth over 20 USD. Getting him for 17 USD was called tremendous value.
Atlanta has no true point guard. McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels share the ball handling.
Atlanta's playoff schedule is 4-4-3 games with a March 28 end. The team has 14 back-to-backs, and resting players is not a concern.
Atlanta is projected to win about 46 games and finish between fourth and eighth in the East.
His Yahoo injury status is Q (Rest).

durable.text: Steals are his elite category and a clear league outlier. His steals totals vary a lot from year to year.
He grew up as a point guard and handles the ball. He can give 5 to 6 assists, and he rebounds well for a guard.
He is a poor shooter and a weak scorer. Threes and FT% are his weakest categories, while his FG% is good for his position.
He is an All-Defense player with excellent defensive metrics.
He is worth much more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: Daniels is a steals specialist who also gives assists, rebounds and a good FG%. That makes him a natural fit for punt FT% and punt 3PM builds. The market is split on his price. His Yahoo average cost is 4.2 USD against a Yahoo value of 16 USD, ESPN prices him at 11.1 USD, and our league paid 28 USD last season. Experts think he is worth 20 USD or more, so anything under that is a buy. Early in the season, check whether his three-point shooting improves on last season's 18%, whether his steals climb back above 2 per game, and whether Lu Dort cuts into his minutes.
